name: 176. Key selection and retries on run-scoped providers (key-pool-selection)
description:
Wire-level pins for key selection within one provider, with no session involved. Each row stands up its own run-scoped custom provider on the OpenAI base. Live keys carry the real credential; dead keys carry a value OpenAI refuses for free. Key weights make every pick deterministic: a weight-0 key is never chosen by ordinary selection beside a weighted one, so a request served on it got there through the behaviour under test.

Rows: (1) a dead key hands the request to its live sibling, attempt trail [dead 401, live]; (2) one dead key at max_retries 1 collapses into 502 upstream_credentials_exhausted; (3) two dead keys at max_retries 1 return OpenAI's raw 401, because walking past the first key went beyond the retry budget; (4) key model filters ([] denies every model, a blacklist wins over '*', a regex entry allows) leave only the key that may serve; (5) a model no key allows is refused with no_key_supports_model; (6) x-bf-api-key selects a key by name, and x-bf-api-key-id wins over it, alone pins thirty requests in a row, is trimmed of spaces, and pins nothing when empty; (7) a pin naming no key, or a key that was deleted, is refused by id and by name when the request has no fallbacks, with no upstream call; (8) a pin on a disabled key, or on a key whose models exclude the model, is refused with no upstream call; (9) a caller's pin is dropped when the request falls back to another provider; (10) a key whose alias names a missing model hands the request to a key whose alias resolves, after the provider's 404; (11) batch calls need a key enabled for batches; (12) a keyless custom provider calls upstream with no key. Each row deletes what it made. Run with FEATURE="key-pool-selection".
